The search turned up Grammy wins for all four artists, mostly from the early 1960s ceremonies:

- **Perry Como** won Best Male Pop Vocal Performance at the 1st Annual Grammys (1959) for "Catch a Falling Star." Honoring recordings released between Aug 31, 1957 and Aug 30, 1958 was the eligibility window.
- **Marty Robbins** won Best Country & Western Performance for "El Paso," which was recognized at the 3rd Annual Grammys in 1961. Winners Announced: April 12, 1961 is the date listed for that ceremony.
- **Ray Charles** won Best Male Pop Vocal Performance at the 3rd Annual Grammys (1961) for "Georgia On My Mind." He also won Best Rhythm & Blues Recording in 1962 for "I Can't Stop Loving You," per Ray Charles received a GRAMMY for Best Rhythm & Blues Recording for "l Can't Stop Loving You."
- **Tony Bennett** won Record of the Year at the 5th Annual Grammys (1963) for "I Left My Heart in San Francisco," which became one of his signature songs.

Two caveats: the popculturemadness page calls Robbins's win a first for a woman in a country category, which I couldn't verify and which looks wrong, so I'd leave it out. Also, the Ray Charles award years differ slightly between sources, so check grammy.com before relying on exact years.
